senses.def: an illegal act; a crime
examples: Driving without a license is a serious offense.
He was arrested for a minor drug offense.

senses.def: the feeling of being upset or insulted by something someone says or does
examples: No offense, but I think your plan won't work.
She took offense at his comment about her accent.

senses.def: the players in a team whose job is to score points
examples: The team's offense scored 35 points in the first half.

note: American spelling is offense; British is offence. In US sports, offense (attack) is the opposite of defense, stressed on the first syllable.

senses.def: rude or insulting in a way that upsets people
examples: The comedian apologized for his offensive jokes.
Many people find that word deeply offensive.

senses.def: a large military attack, or a strong organized effort to achieve something
examples: The army launched a major offensive in the north.
The company began a marketing offensive to win back customers.

note: "Go on the offensive" = start attacking or criticizing instead of defending yourself.

senses.def: to say you are willing to give something to someone or to do something for them
examples: He offered me a ride to the airport.
The hotel offers free breakfast to all guests.

senses.def: a statement that you are willing to do or give something
examples: She accepted a job offer from a tech company in Austin.
Thanks for the offer, but I can manage.

senses.def: a reduced price for a product for a short time
examples: This special offer ends on Sunday.

note: Pattern: offer someone something / offer to do something. Not "offer someone to do something".

senses.def: something that is produced or made available for people to buy, use, watch or enjoy
examples: The band's latest offering is their best album yet.
The restaurant's vegetarian offerings are limited.

senses.def: something given as a gift, especially to God or a church
examples: Villagers left offerings of fruit and flowers at the temple.

note: In finance, an "initial public offering" (IPO) is when a company first sells shares to the public (halka arz).

senses.def: a room or building where people work, usually at desks
examples: I usually get to the office around 8:30.
The company is moving to a new office downtown.

senses.def: an important official position, especially in government
examples: The president has been in office for two years.
She plans to run for office next year.

note: In American English, a doctor's or dentist's place of work is an office (British: surgery).

senses.def: a person in a position of authority in the army, navy or air force
examples: Her father was an officer in the Navy.
The officers gave orders to the soldiers.

senses.def: a police officer
examples: Excuse me, officer, can you tell me where the station is?
Two officers arrived at the scene within minutes.

senses.def: a person with an important position in an organization
examples: She was promoted to chief financial officer last year.

senses.def: approved or done by people in authority, or connected with a position of authority
examples: The official results will be announced tomorrow.
English is the official language of the conference.

senses.def: a person with authority in a government or large organization
examples: Government officials refused to comment on the report.
A city official said the road would reopen on Monday.

note: Officials (yetkililer) are usually government or organization staff; officers are usually in the army or police.

senses.def: to balance the effect of something with something opposite, so that the situation stays the same
examples: Higher fuel prices were offset by lower food costs.
Many travelers pay to offset the carbon emissions from their flights.

senses.def: something that balances or cancels out the effect of something else
examples: The tax cut serves as an offset to rising living costs.

note: Irregular: offset – offset – offset. Often passive: be offset by something.

senses.def: a person's child or children, or an animal's young
examples: Some birds feed their offspring for weeks after they hatch.
Parents naturally want the best for their offspring.

note: Plural is also offspring. Formal or humorous when used about people.

senses.def: many times, or in many cases
examples: How often do you go to the gym?
Teenagers often sleep late on weekends.

note: The t is usually silent: /ˈɔːfn/. "Every so often" = sometimes, not frequently.

senses.def: used to react to something, especially news you did not know, or to show surprise, disappointment or pain
examples: "I got the job!" "Oh, that's wonderful!"
Oh no, I left my wallet at home.

senses.def: used before a short pause, or when adding a comment
examples: Oh, by the way, your mom called.

note: "Oh well" shows you accept a disappointing situation (neyse, napalım).

senses.def: a thick dark liquid found underground, used to make fuel and other products
examples: Oil prices rose sharply after the attack.
The country's economy depends heavily on oil exports.

senses.def: a smooth liquid from plants or animals, used in cooking or for other purposes
examples: Heat a little olive oil in a pan.
I need to change the oil in my car.

senses.def: used to agree to something or to say yes
examples: "Can you pick me up at six?" "OK, no problem."
OK, let's get started.

senses.tr: iyi, sağ salim; idare eder, fena değil
senses.def: safe and well, or acceptable but not especially good
examples: Are you OK? You look pale.
The food was OK, but nothing special.

senses.def: in a satisfactory way
examples: Is your new laptop working OK?

note: Informal. Also spelled okay. "Is it OK if...?" is a common way to ask for permission.

senses.def: having lived for a long time
examples: My grandfather is getting old, but he still walks every day.
She takes care of old people in her neighborhood.

senses.def: of a particular age
examples: How old is your daughter?
Our house is about a hundred years old.

senses.def: having existed or been used for a long time, or from an earlier time
examples: I ran into an old friend from high school.
We sold our old car and bought an electric one.

note: "An old friend" usually means a friend you have known a long time, not an elderly friend. Elder/eldest are used only for family members.

senses.def: not modern; typical of the past and no longer common or fashionable
examples: My parents still have an old-fashioned phone with a cord.
He has some old-fashioned ideas about women working.

senses.def: traditional, in a way that people like
examples: The bakery sells good, old-fashioned apple pie.

note: Opposite: modern, up to date. "Good old-fashioned" is positive.

senses.def: touching or supported by a surface
examples: Your keys are on the kitchen table.
There's a spider on the wall.

senses.def: used with days and dates, topics, and means of communication
examples: We're meeting on Friday.
She wrote a book on climate change.

senses.def: working or switched on, being worn, or continuing
examples: Is the oven on?
Put your coat on; it's cold outside.

note: Use on for days and dates (on Monday, on May 3), in for months and years, at for clock times.

senses.def: one time only
examples: I've only been to New York once.
We meet once a month to discuss the project.

senses.def: at some time in the past
examples: This building was once a factory.

senses.def: as soon as; after
examples: Once you've finished your homework, you can watch TV.
It's easy once you know how.

note: "At once" = immediately or at the same time. "Once and for all" = finally and completely (ilk ve son kez).

senses.def: the number 1
examples: I have one brother and two sisters.
Only one of the candidates passed the test.

senses.def: used to mean a particular person, thing or time that is not named
examples: One day I'd like to live by the ocean.

senses.def: used instead of repeating a noun that has already been mentioned
examples: I don't like the red shirt; I prefer the blue one.
Which one do you want?

note: "The blue one / the old ones": English needs one(s) here, while Turkish just says "maviyi".

senses.def: continuing to exist or develop; not finished
examples: Police say the investigation is ongoing.
Training is an ongoing process, not a one-time event.

note: Common in news and business English.

senses.def: a round vegetable with many layers and a strong smell and taste
examples: Chop the onion and fry it until it's golden.
Cutting onions always makes me cry.

note: In American English, green onions are what British people call spring onions (taze soğan).

senses.def: available on or done using the internet
examples: She runs an online store that sells handmade jewelry.
Online classes became common during the pandemic.

senses.def: using the internet, or onto the internet
examples: I bought my plane tickets online.
He spends hours online every evening.

note: Opposite: offline. "Come online" can also mean that a new system starts working.

senses.def: no one or nothing except; no more than
examples: The store only accepts cash.
It only takes ten minutes to get there by bike.

senses.def: used to say that there is no other person or thing of the same kind
examples: She was the only person who noticed the mistake.
I'm an only child, so I have no brothers or sisters.

senses.def: (informal) except that; but
examples: I'd love to come, only I have to work late.

note: Position matters: "Only I saw her" vs "I only saw her" vs "I saw only her" have different meanings. "If only" expresses a wish (keşke).

senses.def: used to show movement to a position on a surface
examples: The cat jumped onto the kitchen counter.
Pour the sauce onto the pasta.

senses.def: (informal) aware of what someone is doing, especially something wrong
examples: The police are onto him, so he'd better be careful.

note: Onto shows movement (jump onto the bed); on shows position (sit on the bed). "Be onto something" = have found something important.

senses.def: not closed, so that people or things can go through, or ready for business
examples: Someone left the window open all night.
Is the pharmacy open on Sundays?

senses.def: honest and willing to talk, or willing to consider new ideas
examples: She's very open about her struggles with anxiety.
I'm open to suggestions.

senses.def: to move something so it is no longer closed, or to start operating
examples: Can you open the door for me?
The new library opens next month.

senses.def: a space or hole that something can pass through
examples: The dog escaped through an opening in the fence.

senses.def: the beginning of something, or a ceremony to start a new building, business or event
examples: Hundreds of people came to the opening of the new museum.
The movie's opening was a little slow.

senses.def: a job that is available, or a good opportunity
examples: There are several openings for nurses at the clinic.

senses.def: without hiding your feelings, opinions or information
examples: He spoke openly about his divorce in the interview.
Few employees dared to openly criticize the boss.

senses.def: a drama in which most or all of the words are sung to music, or this kind of art
examples: We saw a wonderful opera at the Met last night.
She trained as an opera singer in Italy.

note: "Soap opera" = a TV drama series about the daily lives of characters (dizi, pembe dizi).

senses.def: to work or function in a particular way, or to do business
examples: The company operates in more than 40 countries.
Most smartphones operate on rechargeable batteries.

senses.def: to use and control a machine
examples: You need special training to operate a crane.

senses.def: to cut open someone's body in order to repair or remove a damaged part
examples: Surgeons operated on her knee last week.

note: For surgery, use operate ON someone.

senses.def: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts open the body to remove or repair a part
examples: He had an operation on his back last year.
The operation took four hours.

senses.def: an organized activity involving many people, especially soldiers or police
examples: The rescue operation continued through the night.

senses.def: the way something works, or the fact of being active
examples: The new factory will be in operation by next spring.

note: American speakers often say surgery rather than "an operation": "He had knee surgery."

senses.def: connected with the way a business, machine or system works
examples: The company is cutting operational costs to save money.
We faced several operational problems in the first year.

senses.def: working and ready to be used
examples: The new airport terminal will be fully operational by June.

senses.def: a person who works a machine or piece of equipment
examples: The crane operator lifted the steel beams into place.

senses.def: a company that runs a particular business or service
examples: The tour operator canceled our trip because of the storm.
Mobile phone operators are raising their prices.

senses.def: a person who works at a telephone exchange and connects calls
examples: I called the operator to ask for the number.

senses.def: what you think or feel about something, rather than a fact
examples: In my opinion, the movie was too long.
Public opinion has turned against the war.

note: Say "in my opinion", not "according to me". "A second opinion" is advice from another expert, especially a doctor.

senses.def: a person you play, compete or fight against
examples: She beat her opponent in straight sets.
The senator attacked his opponent's record on taxes.

senses.def: a person who disagrees with an idea or plan and tries to stop it
examples: Opponents of the new law say it will hurt small businesses.

senses.def: a time or situation in which it is possible to do something you want
examples: Studying abroad was a great opportunity to learn Spanish.
I'd like to take this opportunity to thank my team.

note: Pattern: an opportunity to do something / for something / of doing something.

senses.def: to disagree strongly with a plan, policy or idea and try to stop it
examples: Many parents oppose the plan to close the school.
The bill was opposed by both parties.

note: Transitive: oppose something (not "oppose to something"). Compare: be opposed to something.

senses.def: strongly disagreeing with something
examples: Most residents are opposed to the new highway.
I'm not opposed to the idea, but we need more details.

note: "Be opposed to" + noun/-ing. "As opposed to" = rather than, in contrast with ("-in aksine").

senses.def: completely different, or on the other side or in the other direction
examples: The two brothers have opposite personalities.
The bus was going in the opposite direction.

senses.def: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another
examples: "Hot" is the opposite of "cold."
I thought he'd be shy, but he was the exact opposite.

senses.def: on the other side of an area from someone or something, facing them
examples: The bank is opposite the post office.

senses.def: on the other side, facing
examples: She sat down opposite and smiled at me.

note: As a preposition, Americans often prefer "across from" (the bank is across from the post office).

senses.def: strong disagreement with something, usually with the aim of stopping it
examples: There was strong opposition to the new tax.
The plan met with fierce opposition from environmental groups.

senses.def: the main political parties not in government, or the people you are competing against
examples: The opposition accused the government of hiding the truth.

senses.def: to choose one thing or course of action instead of another
examples: Many students opt for online classes because they're cheaper.
She opted to take the train instead of flying.

note: "Opt out" = choose not to take part (e.g., opt out of emails); "opt in" = choose to take part.

senses.def: connected with sight or with light and how it is used to see
examples: The lines look curved, but it's just an optical illusion.
The lab makes optical instruments such as microscopes.

note: "Optical illusion" = göz yanılması.

senses.def: a feeling that good things will happen and things will be successful
examples: There is growing optimism that the economy will recover.
She faced her illness with remarkable optimism.

note: Opposite: pessimism.

senses.def: expecting good things to happen or something to be successful
examples: Doctors are optimistic that she will make a full recovery.
I'm optimistic about our chances in the final.

note: Opposite: pessimistic. Pattern: optimistic about something / optimistic that...

senses.def: something you can choose, or the freedom to choose
examples: We have two options: take the bus or walk.
Selling the house is not an option for us.

note: "Have no option but to" = be forced to (başka çaresi olmamak).

senses.def: used to connect possibilities or alternatives
examples: Would you like coffee or tea?
You can pay by card or in cash.

senses.def: used to say what will happen if something is not done
examples: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus.

senses.def: used after a negative to mean "and not"
examples: He doesn't smoke or drink.

note: "Or so" = approximately (an hour or so). In negatives, English uses or, not nor: "I don't eat meat or fish."

senses.def: spoken rather than written
examples: We have an oral exam in French next week.
The story was passed down through oral tradition.

senses.def: connected with the mouth, or taken by mouth
examples: Good oral hygiene helps prevent gum disease.

note: Opposite of the first meaning: written.

senses.def: a round, juicy citrus fruit with a thick skin
examples: I squeeze fresh oranges for juice every morning.
She peeled an orange and shared it with her son.

senses.def: having a color between red and yellow
examples: The workers wore bright orange vests.

senses.def: the color between red and yellow
examples: The sky turned a deep orange at sunset.

note: One word, two Turkish translations: portakal (the fruit) and turuncu (the color).

senses.def: a large group of musicians who play different instruments together, led by a conductor
examples: She plays the violin in the city's symphony orchestra.
The orchestra performed a program of Mozart and Beethoven.

note: In US theaters, "the orchestra" also means the seats on the main floor (British: the stalls).

senses.def: the way things are arranged in relation to each other, or a state of being neat and organized
examples: The names are listed in alphabetical order.
The police were called to restore order.

senses.def: an instruction from someone in authority, or a request for goods or food
examples: The soldiers were given orders to retreat.
Your order will arrive within three days.

senses.def: to ask for food, drinks or goods to be brought or sent to you
examples: Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?

senses.def: to tell someone to do something, using your authority
examples: The judge ordered the company to pay damages.

note: "In order to" = so that you can (-mek için). "Out of order" = not working (bozuk).

senses.def: normal or usual; not special or different in any way
examples: It was just an ordinary Tuesday until the phone rang.
Ordinary people can't afford to live in this neighborhood.

note: "Out of the ordinary" = unusual (alışılmışın dışında).

senses.def: a part of the body or a plant that has a particular job, such as the heart or a leaf
examples: The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
Thousands of patients are waiting for an organ transplant.

senses.def: a large musical instrument with pipes and keys, often found in churches
examples: She played the organ at her sister's wedding.
